title: Through my fault
hook: the whole church admits it has sinned and asks each other for prayer

segments.voice: Yesterday, the entrance: a procession, a kissed altar, a greeting. Your line was we gather first. Did you arrive early anywhere? Day one hundred and five.

Imagine a meeting at work that starts like this. Everyone stands up, the boss included, and says out loud, together: I've messed up. In what I thought, what I said, what I did, and what I didn't do. It's my fault. Then everyone turns to the people around them and says: please pray for me. It would be the strangest meeting of your life. And it's roughly what happens in the first three minutes of a Catholic Mass, every Sunday, in every language, all over the world. Right after the greeting, before a single reading, the whole church owns up. Today's word is the prayer they say.
screen: `A MEETING THAT STARTS WITH SORRY.` → `EVERYONE, THE BOSS INCLUDED.` → `THE FIRST THREE MINUTES OF MASS.`

segments.voice: It's called the Confiteor, from its first word in Latin: I confess. The priest invites everyone to call their sins to mind, and there's a short silence. Then priest and people together say they confess to almighty God, and to each other, that they have greatly sinned, in their thoughts and in their words, in what they have done and in what they have failed to do. That last part is sharp. Not just the wrong things. The good things left undone. Then comes the famous line, in the old Latin: mea culpa, mea culpa, mea maxima culpa. Through my fault, through my fault, through my most grievous fault. And as they say it, many people strike their chest with a closed hand. That gesture is from a story Jesus told. A tax collector stands at the back of the Temple, won't even lift his eyes, beats his breast and says, in the Douay-Rheims: "O God, be merciful to me a sinner." Jesus says that man went home right with God. Then the Confiteor turns outward. Everyone asks Mary, the angels and the saints, and you, my brothers and sisters, to pray for me. You confess to the people beside you, and then you ask them for help. Nobody stands above anybody. The priest says it too. The Church is clear that this isn't the sacrament of confession. It doesn't replace that. It's a way of starting honestly. Looking back over this week, from bending the knee to the Angelus to the entrance, the body keeps saying things before words do. Here, it's a fist on the chest.
screen: `CONFITEOR: I CONFESS.` · `DONE, AND FAILED TO DO.` · `MEA CULPA, AND A FIST ON THE CHEST.` · `PRAY FOR ME, BROTHERS AND SISTERS.` · then, large: `O GOD, BE MERCIFUL TO ME A SINNER.`

segments.voice: Here's the practice: one honest moment. Settle, and breathe. Think back over the last day or two. Not to punish yourself. Just to see clearly. One thing you did that you wish you hadn't. One thing you left undone. If you're Catholic, or you'd like to, you can strike your chest gently, once, the way the tax collector did. If you pray, you can use his words. If not, just name it, and set it down. The bell holds the time.
Confiteor. I confess: the prayer at the start of Mass where everyone admits their sins and asks each other for prayer. Today's word.
Your line: we all begin as sinners. Today, when you're tempted to feel above someone, remember that a whole church starts every Sunday by saying my fault. Day one hundred and five.

howItsDone: At the start of most Masses, after a brief silence, priest and people pray the Confiteor together, many striking their breast at 'through my fault'; it is one of several forms of the penitential act and does not replace the sacrament of confession.

fork.reveal: he beat his breast and said: "O God, be merciful to me a sinner." Jesus says he went home right with God. the fist on the chest at Mass comes from him.

The English Confiteor (ICEL 2011) is paraphrased, not quoted; 'you, my brothers and sisters, to pray for me' is a near-quote spoken without quotation marks. A Keeper should confirm this short echo is acceptable or ask for further paraphrase.
GIRM 51: the penitential act 'lacks the efficacy of the Sacrament of Penance'. Confirm the phrasing.
The Confiteor is one of three forms of the penitential act (and may be replaced by the sprinkling rite on Sundays); the hook's 'every Sunday' is a simplification. Confirm.
